clue.text: A table on the Orient Express?

parts.note: taken as written
a board is a table, as in the festive board

explanation.surface: A puzzled diner wonders whether a particular dining table is to be found on the famous luxury train.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is an example: being on any train is being aboard it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone riding a train or ship is said to be travelling aboard it, so this prepositional phrase works as an example.

clue.text: Difficult problem bar trainees sorted

indicators.note: sorted suggests letters being put into a new order, like papers rearranged on a desk

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Apprentice bartenders present the pub with a tricky problem that must be sorted out.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzle that tests the mind is a hard question, commonly called by this informal compound noun.

clue.text: US soldier tucking into brew in Mobile

indicators.note: tucking into means getting inside something else, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: ale is a brewed beer
GI is the standard term for an American serviceman

explanation.surface: An American soldier helps himself to a beer in the city of Mobile, Alabama.
explanation.walkthrough: Mobile looks like the Alabama city, but lower-cased in sense it means nimble, able to move freely.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone mobile moves about easily and quickly, which is a synonym for nimble and lithe.

clue.text: Result of ridicule? Republican becomes cold!

indicators.note: becomes says one letter turns into another, swapping its place in the word

parts.note: derision is mockery or ridicule
R is the abbreviation for Republican
C stands for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A Republican politician, mocked by the press, turns frosty in reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: DERISION has its R swapped for C to give DECISION.
explanation.definitionFit: A verdict or ruling reached at the end of deliberation is its outcome, as in the result of a match.

clue.text: Boisterous rubbish coach enters into

indicators.note: enters into means going inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: rot means nonsense, rubbish
a coach is a long-distance bus

explanation.surface: A rowdy crowd piles into a terrible coach on a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Robust means vigorous and full of energy, which loosely overlaps with rowdy, lively, unrestrained behaviour.

clue.text: Singer associated with Brown and Plant

parts.note: an informer who sings to the police is a rat
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: It reads like a question about a vocalist linked with the rock stars Robert Plant and James Brown.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Plant the Led Zeppelin singer is a red herring: Plant is the definition, and singer is slang for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattan is a climbing palm whose canes are used for furniture and wickerwork, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Catholic dude demolishes head of school on TV

parts.note: catholic, in lower-case sense, means wide-ranging or broad, as in catholic tastes

indicators.note: demolishing something knocks it apart so the pieces can be rebuilt differently

parts.note: cat is old jazz slang for a cool guy

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of school

explanation.surface: A Catholic man wrecks the career of a headmaster on a television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Catholic with a capital pretends to be about religion; the setter uses its general sense of broad.
explanation.definitionFit: Something being transmitted on television is being aired, so the adjective broadcast fits a programme shown on TV.

clue.text: Musical genre Mark heard on radio

indicators.note: on the radio we only hear words, so it is the sound that counts not spelling

parts.note: a scar is a mark on the skin; in a non-rhotic British accent it sounds like the genre

explanation.surface: Someone named Mark is heard on the radio talking about a style of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Ska is a Jamaican music style, forerunner of reggae, with an offbeat rhythm.

clue.text: Concoct happy lectures? I might!

indicators.note: to concoct is to cook up from ingredients, so these letters are mixed into something new

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A speaker boasts that they could cook up cheerful lessons on demand.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a stand-in teacher might well invent jolly lessons. In Britain a supply teacher is what Americans call a substitute teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A temporary stand-in covering absent staff in schools might well improvise cheerful lessons for a class.

clue.text: A spirit seen by mansion in Battle

parts.note: taken as written
gin is a spirit, the drink
a court is a stately house, as in Hampton Court

explanation.surface: A ghost is spotted near a grand house in the town of Battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Battle is a real English town in Sussex, named after the 1066 fight, which makes the capital letter innocent-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Agincourt was the famous 1415 victory of Henry V over the French, a celebrated historic battle.

clue.text: Old boy and knight drinking a port

indicators.note: drinking takes something inside, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
N is knight in chess notation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A former pupil and a knight share a glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: Port looks like the wine they are drinking, but it is the definition, a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban is a harbour town on the west coast of Scotland, a ferry port for the islands.

clue.text: Beat-up cars heading off for city abroad

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its front, and off means it is taken away

parts.note: a banger is British slang for an old, battered car

explanation.surface: Battered old cars set off on a trip to a foreign city.
explanation.walkthrough: BANGERS loses its B to leave ANGERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Angers is a city in the Loire valley in western France, so foreign from the British setter's viewpoint.

clue.text: Make light of ultimately crap yield

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of crap
to lay down arms is to surrender, to yield

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a terrible harvest as nothing to worry about.
explanation.definitionFit: To minimise or downplay something is to treat it as less important than it is.

clue.text: A crew's route up the Thames?

definitions.note: the Thames is an example of the answer, hence the question mark

indicators.note: up can mean in disorder or out of sorts, as when things are all up in the air

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A rowing crew follows its course upstream along London's river, as in the Boat Race.
explanation.walkthrough: Up looks like the direction of travel on the river, but it signals a jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a natural channel along which water flows, so the Thames is one example of this.

clue.text: Sorry I've messed up making changes

indicators.note: something messed up is jumbled, so the letters come out in a different order

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: An apologetic editor admits a mistake while altering a document.
explanation.definitionFit: A revisory adjective describes something concerned with revision, the act of altering or amending a text.

clue.text: Dead hot article on current lover

parts.note: hot means fashionable, which is in
an is the indefinite article
I is the physics symbol for electric current
a mate is a partner or lover

explanation.surface: A lurid tabloid headline about a dead body found on top of a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without life, never living, is lifeless, which overlaps with dead in the sense of not alive.

clue.text: One against physician tickling nurses

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold something close, so the letters are cradled inside the phrase

parts.note: found inside the end of physician and the start of tickling

explanation.surface: A doctor who refuses to tickle patients is opposed to the idea.
explanation.walkthrough: Nurses looks like the hospital staff alongside the physician, but it is the verb meaning holds.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti is an opponent, a person who stands opposed to a policy or proposal.

clue.text: Book by poet and journalist Spooner's mentioned

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so what he said is the swap

parts.note: a bard is a poet and a hack a journalist; swapping their opening sounds gives the result

explanation.surface: A volume written by someone who is both poet and reporter, as reported by Spooner.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardback is a book bound in stiff covers, so it is one form a published volume takes.

clue.text: When army leader seizes one big piece of ground!

indicators.note: to seize is to grab and hold, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of army
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A general captures a vast territory, exclaimed with some pride.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest continent, so it is indeed a very large landmass, said with wry understatement.

clue.text: We take advantage of retired players

definitions.note: the answer is a plural noun; the clue lets the exactors speak for themselves

parts.note: ex means former, no longer in post
players in the theatre are actors

explanation.surface: Former performers confess to exploiting someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactors are people who demand or extort payment, extracting from others what they can.

clue.text: Eat around six? That's wonderful!

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped about the other

parts.note: to dine is to eat a meal
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An invitation to dinner at six o'clock is greeted with delight.
explanation.definitionFit: Divine is used informally to praise something as heavenly or delightful, a gushing term of approval.

clue.text: Highly-clever sort in Arabic novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A brilliant person appears in a book written in Arabic.
explanation.walkthrough: Novel looks like a book in Arabic, but it is the adjective new.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainiac is informal slang for a very intelligent person, a genius or egghead.

clue.text: Cook bones?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: falsify, as in cooking the books
second meaning: sawbones is slang for a surgeon or medic

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an instruction to make stock from bones; bones is short for sawbones, slang for a medic.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor figures is to tamper with them, and a sawbones is a physician, hence both meanings.

clue.text: Worry about daughter in revolutionary group

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: care means worry or anxiety
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent frets over their daughter joining a band of radicals.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadre is a trained core of activists, especially in a communist or revolutionary party.

clue.text: It's said I possess a bit of Scottish land

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the sound of the words counts rather than their letters

parts.note: to possess is to own

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of owning a small Scottish plot.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland, famous for its abbey.

clue.text: Saggy and wrinkled, but daring to go topless

indicators.note: topless means without a top, and in a down entry the top is the first letter

parts.note: bold means daring

explanation.surface: An elderly person is brave enough to sunbathe without a top on.
explanation.walkthrough: BOLD loses its first letter to leave OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagging skin and wrinkles are the signs of age, so the phrase describes someone elderly.

clue.text: Foreign citizen in care led astray

indicators.note: going astray is wandering off course, so the letters stray out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A foreign national in local authority care is misled.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Iceland is a national of a country other than Britain, hence foreign from the setter's view.

clue.text: Stick to a present with inset diamonds

indicators.note: something inset is set within, so one piece goes inside the rest

parts.note: taken as written
present means here, in attendance
D is diamonds, the card suit

explanation.surface: A shopper settles on a gift with diamonds set into it.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling or be glued firmly, which is what sticking means.

clue.text: Caretaker of tower to meet Her Maj

parts.note: a keep is the main tower of a castle
ER is the Queen, Elizabeth Regina; Her Maj is British slang for Her Majesty

explanation.surface: The custodian of a castle tower is presented to the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A keeper looks after something, such as a zoo animal or museum, so the role overlaps with custodian.
